headline: South Asia: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
- Western Russia: Russia attacks Ukraine with 148 drones, most of them jet-powered, strikes recorded at 24 locations.
- Africa: Sudan: Drone Attack Kills Two in North Darfur As Red Crescent Volunteer Killed in Blue Nile.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: What is the US Army doing in Panama? A bit of everything..
- Military Times, one hour ago: What is the US Army doing in Panama? A bit of everything..
As Washington shifts its attention toward the Western Hemisphere, a reinvigorated jungle school is just one part of the evolving U.S. presence in Panama.
- Military Times, 15 hours ago: US Army eyes developing soldier-worn drone detection gear.
The Army is in the early stages of developing and testing a wearable or lightweight device that could alert soldiers to the presence of hostile drones.
The Caribbean - bottom line: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
A 19-year-old man has been charged with three counts of murder in connection with last Friday’s deadly attack on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, which claimed the lives of two women and a one-year-old boy. The accused, Dante Davis, who has addresses on Spanish Town Road and Kidd Lane in Kingston 13, is also facing charges of conspiracy to commit murder, arson, conspiracy to commit arson, possession of a prohibited weapon, unauthorised possession of ammunition and using a firearm to commit a felony.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russia attacks Ukraine with 148 drones, most of them jet-powered, strikes recorded at 24 locations.
Russia attacked Ukraine with 148 drones overnight, most of them jet-powered. Air defence brought down 114 UAVs, and strikes were recorded at 24 locations.

- The Moscow Times, 23 hours ago: Ukraine Says Missile Strike Destroyed 6 Russian Warplanes at Voronezh Airfield.

- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russian Banderol missiles attack Bakhmach in Chernihiv Oblast: several injured, extensive damage reported – photos.
Russian forces attacked the city of Bakhmach in Chernihiv Oblast with Banderol drone-launched cruise missiles on the morning of 16 October, causing extensive damage and leaving four people in need of medical treatment.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Trump slams Ukraine’s decision to resume energy strikes as a ‘disgrace’.
- Politico Europe, one hour ago: Trump slams Ukraine’s decision to resume energy strikes as a ‘disgrace’.
Ukraine had paused strikes on Russian energy infrastructure after Trump’s ceasefire announcement.
- Balkan Insight, 5 hours ago: Democracy Digest: Polish Man Charged With Plotting to Kill PM, Suspected Saboteurs Arrested.

- Balkan Insight, 5 hours ago: ‘Invisible Human Engine’: Book Goes Behind Courtroom Battles at Yugoslav Tribunal.
A groundbreaking book about the UN’s tribunal in The Hague shifts the focus from war criminals on trial to the hidden workforce that powered the court.
- Politico Europe, 8 hours ago: Are the Brexit wars back?.
Customs union, single market, rejoin, second referendum. It’s all feeling a little Ground Hog day in Westminster after Andy Burnham reopened the Europe question at Labour Party conference. Hosts Sascha O’Sullivan and Pat Baker find out how the row over Europe will play out in the next few years, with Reform MP Danny Kruger and […]

Africa - bottom line: Sudan: Drone Attack Kills Two in North Darfur As Red Crescent Volunteer Killed in Blue Nile.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 6 hours ago: Sudan: Drone Attack Kills Two in North Darfur As Red Crescent Volunteer Killed in Blue Nile.
[Dabanga] Furawiya / Karnoi / El Tina / Umm Darfa / El Rosei -- Drone attack in Furawiya area of North Darfur kills two and injures eight, while a Red Crescent volunteer dies in a bombing in Blue Nile and South Darfur authorities impose sweeping emergency measures.
- Africanews, 16 hours ago: Houthis struck Riyadh airport 20 times in October, Saudi-led coalition says.
Yemen’s Houthi rebels have struck Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport 20 times since the start of October. A spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition said the attacks involved 10 drones, four ballistic missiles, four cruise missiles and two unidentified projectiles.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, one hour ago: Nigeria: Soldiers, Terrorists Killed in Midnight Terror Attack On Borno Military Base.
[Premium Times] Sources said 15 soldiers and five members of the Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF) were killed in the encounter.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 20 hours ago: Somalia: Somali Parliamentary Speaker Marks Ninth Anniversary of Mogadishu Truck Bombing.
[Shabelle] Mogadishu -- Somalia's parliamentary speaker, Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur Jama, on Wednesday attended a commemoration at the Soobe intersection in Mogadishu marking the ninth anniversary of a devastating truck bombing that killed hundreds of people.

- Al Jazeera - Middle East, just now: Poland scrambles fighter jets as Russia strikes western Ukraine.

Angry families and political supporters packed the courtroom as Sibeko faced charges linked to a shooting that killed four people and wounded three others.

[Scrolla] The National Prosecuting Authority says no warrant was issued and that it takes no instructions from political parties or public office holders. KwaZulu-Natal police say they have no trace of any case registered against the two and urge activists not to make reckless statements.

[Namibian] The Ministry of Health and Social Services has warned the public against confusing foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) which affects animals, with hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) which commonly affects children.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its “sovereignty, security and territorial integrity” amid a recent escalation in Houthi attacks. According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the premier made the remarks during a meeting with newly appointed Saudi Ambassador Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy. He welcomed the envoy to Pakistan and congratulated him on assuming his new responsibilities.
- The Hindu - International, one hour ago: Airstrikes, artillery hit north Ethiopia as government and rebels clash, sources say.
Air attacks killed at least 17 people northwest of Tigray’s capital Mekelle — which federal government forces took over the weekend — according to a bulletin circulated among humanitarian groups
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: Trump banking on ‘swift end’ of Iran war to bring down fuel prices.
• Pezeshkian decries US blockade, insists ‘military force’ will not compel Tehran into submission • Washington weighs using ‘Mother Of All Bombs’ against Iranian energy sites, CNN reports WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump once again predicted a swift end to the war with Iran, and a sharp drop in oil prices once the conflict concludes, even as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian warned that military action cannot force them into submission. “The Iran war will end very soon … Soon, as they want it to end,” Trump told reporters in Montana.
- The Hindu - International, 4 hours ago: Drone strikes in the Black Sea raise fears of Russian escalation to test NATO's response.
The attacks in the two countries' exclusive economic zones threaten a global shipping route and have left two people dead, with at least 25 still missing. They also run the risk of drawing other countries directly into the war for Ukraine
India - bottom line: Spotting drones before it's too late: US Army eyes wearable detection tech.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Spotting drones before it's too late: US Army eyes wearable detection tech.
The US Army is currently examining innovative wearable tech that provides soldiers with real-time alerts about incoming hostile drones during engagements. This compact sensor leverages unique acoustic signatures for immediate warnings, prioritizing soldier safety without burdening them with extra gear. Insights from the ongoing conflict in Ukraine underscore the necessity of advanced drone detection systems, ultimately aiming to bolster the effectiveness and protection of troops on the front lines.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Missiles, Drones, 'Battle-Hardened Group': Houthis' Arsenal Against Saudi.
The trigger for their return to hostilities, after a four-year truce, was a Saudi bombardment of the airport at Sanaa, Yemen's capital, in July.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: US holds secret Myanmar talks as rare earth minerals at stake.
Renewed talks between the U.S. and Myanmar's military-backed rulers signal strategic interests in rare-earth resources. These discussions focused on securing the release of an American businessman and addressing online scams. Engagement follows Myanmar's civil war, which has led to extensive displacement and control challenges. Myanmar's Kachin State is crucial for heavy rare-earth minerals but is fraught with conflict.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: A mothership for drones, a testbed for weapons: What INS Samarthak brings to Indian Navy.
INS Samarthak has been commissioned as a multi-purpose vessel by the Indian Navy at the Karwar naval base. The ship, with various operational capabilities, is designed to support future Navy missions and technology trials. It can be utilized for tasks ranging from humanitarian assistance to maritime surveillance and environmental protection. Developed by Larsen and Toubro, this vessel significantly incorporates indigenous content in its construction.
Asia - bottom line: EU rallies around Zelensky as rift widens with Trump over Russia energy strikes.
- South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: EU rallies around Zelensky as rift widens with Trump over Russia energy strikes.
European leaders on Friday rallied around Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky as Kyiv’s ties with US President Donald Trump have nosedived and worries grow that US leader is increasingly siding with Russia. Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since last week, when Trump eased sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets. North Korea’s apparent use of different launch methods to fire two types of cruise missiles from a tactical nuclear-capable submarine raises fresh questions about the operational readiness of its growing undersea arsenal, observers have said. The North’s official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said on Thursday the country had “test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles” off its eastern coast. For nearly five decades, the Hong Kong Chinese Orchestra has worked to bring its music to a wider audience, including people who might never have considered entering a concert hall. Executive director Celina Chin Man-wah said the orchestra had long sought to ensure Chinese music was not seen as distant, formal or difficult to understand. That has meant commissioning new works, exploring different musical styles and developing programmes for younger audiences. “We cannot rely on the old...

Illinois authorities believe a 19-year-old man charged with planning a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in suburban Chicago entered the building’s car park on Sunday, hours before police arrested him near his home after receiving a tip about the alleged attack plan. Authorities announced Wednesday that they had arrested Alexandros Paporakis and provided the additional detail about his suspected movement during a news conference Thursday.
